verdict.rationale: three.js has very large adoption: about 12.2M weekly npm downloads, an official examples gallery and a manual. It also publishes an llms.txt with an explicit 'Instructions for Large Language Models' section and a 363 KB llms-full.txt, which supports the well-documented, widely-seen-examples part of the story. The 'stable API' part is undercut, though: the project is still on 0.x with a per-release migration guide (e.g. 185→186). Its own llms.txt has to steer models away from 'Old CDN Patterns' toward import maps and WebGPU/TSL, which implies models' learned examples are often out of date. missing for 10: evidence of API stability across versions, hands-on proof that LLM-generated code works on first try, per-page static/markdown doc URLs (manual .md returns 404), accurate TypeScript signatures.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, LLM-generated code mostly works on the first try — stable, well-documented APIs with abundant public examples the models have seen
